title: Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Bill
what_it_is: Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Bill

sections.label: Gallup law and order ranking
sections.summary: Singapore was ranked first in the Gallup Global Law and Order Report 2020 for the sixth year running.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In the most recent Gallup Global Law and Order Report 2020, we were ranked first, for the sixth year running.

sections.label: GEW licence numbers doubling
sections.summary: Total GEW licences more than doubled from around 2,000 in 2010 to more than 4,000 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Since then, the total number of GEW licences has more than doubled, from around 2,000 in 2010 to more than 4,000 in 2020.

sections.label: Guns Explosives Weapons Control Bill
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to replace the Arms and Explosives Act, Explosive Substances Act and Dangerous Fireworks Act, and amend other GEW-related Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Bill before this House seeks to replace the Arms and Explosives Act, the Explosive Substances Act and the Dangerous Fireworks Act, and make consequential amendments to other GEW-related Acts.

sections.label: Maximum fines for guns explosives
sections.summary: The Bill raises maximum fines for guns and explosives to match those for EPs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Bill therefore raises the maximum fines for guns and explosives to match those for EPs.

sections.label: 3D-printed gun licensing
sections.summary: Clause 13 requires a licence to make a 3D-printed gun or major gun part, and makes possessing a digital blueprint without a licence an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 13 provides that a person who wants to make a 3D-printed gun or major part of a gun by an additive manufacturing process using a 3D printer or electronic milling machine will need a licence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Without a licence, the mere possession of a digital blueprint of a gun or gun part will be an offence.

sections.label: Control over GEW vehicles
sections.summary: Clause 5 treats a person who has control over or operates a vehicle or vessel carrying GEW, even remotely, as possessing the GEW.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 5 addresses the threat by making it clear that a person who has control over or operates a vehicle or vessel carrying GEW, even if via remote control, is treated as possessing the GEW.

sections.label: Class licence for air guns
sections.summary: Clauses 56 to 58 introduce a class licence system for students handling air guns in school CCAs, replacing individual licences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, students who handle air guns as part of their co-curricular activities (CCAs) in schools, generally do so in the campus, in the compound, which is a relatively secure setting, but some safety and security measures are still needed to prevent misuse or mishandling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Therefore, clauses 56 to 58 introduce a class licence system that will work in lieu of individual licences.

sections.label: Licensing Officer suspending class licence
sections.summary: Clause 66 lets the Licensing Officer suspend or disapply a class licence for a specific class licensee on stated grounds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Conversely, under clause 66, the Licensing Officer has the power to suspend or disapply the class licence with respect to a specific class licensee if the LO is satisfied that, inter alia, the class licensee has contravened class licence conditions, is convicted of an offence in a GEW-related Act, or if it is in the public interest or national security of Singapore to do so.

sections.label: Controls for specified weapons
sections.summary: Clauses 29 to 35 create separate controls, offences and penalties for specified weapons, reflecting their lower risk than guns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clauses 29 to 35 create and set out a distinct set of controls, offences and penalties for the specified weapons, to reflect the lower risk they pose vis-à-vis guns and major gun parts.

sections.label: Tighter licence conditions process
sections.summary: The Licensing Officer must revoke and reissue a licence to impose tighter conditions, and cannot tighten conditions on some errant licensees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: If the LO needs to impose tighter conditions on the licensee, for example, to deal with changes in the operating environment, the LO must first revoke and then reissue the license.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Also, the LO cannot impose tighter conditions on an errant licensee whose breach may not warrant licence suspension or revocation.

sections.label: Criminalising regulatory breaches
sections.summary: The Bill criminalises regulatory breaches, leaves criminal intent to other Acts with heavier punishments, and repeals the Explosive Substances Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Moving forward, regulatory breaches like non-compliance with licence conditions or unlicensed activities will be criminalised under the Bill, whereas actions with criminal intent will be offences under the other Acts and will carry heavier punishments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Bill also repeals the Explosive Substances Act, as there are similar offences relating to explosive substances in the CESOWA, such as possession and use of explosive substances with criminal intent.

sections.label: Security clearance for licensees
sections.summary: The Bill applies the current security clearance regime to licensees, their management and certain key personnel called special workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: One of these practices is the current security clearance regime, and which the Bill will apply to licensees and their management, and certain key personnel engaging in regulated activities, called special workers.

sections.label: Offences for licensees and close associates
sections.summary: Clause 47 makes it an offence for a licensee to let a non-security-cleared worker handle GEW, and clause 48 requires licensees to inform the LO within seven days of a person becoming a close associate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In particular, clause 47 makes it an offence if a licensee allows a worker who is not security cleared to handle GEW.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To guard against persons who are not licensees but may have significant influence over an entity engaged in GEW regulated activities, clause 48 makes it an offence if a licensee fails to inform the LO within seven days of a person becoming a close associate.

sections.label: Cutting off digital gun blueprints
sections.summary: The speaker says besides criminalising unauthorised possession of digital blueprints for guns, the source where such blueprints get downloaded must be proactively cut off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In addition to criminalising the unauthorised possession of digital blueprints for guns, we would also need to proactively cut off the source where such blueprints get downloaded.

sections.label: Licensing industrial-grade 3D printer imports
sections.summary: The Ministry could consider imposing a licensing requirement on those who import industrial-grade 3D printers, as such devices could 3D-print a fully functioning gun.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the Ministry could consider imposing a licensing requirement on those who import industrial-grade 3D printers, as such devices have the potential to 3D-print a fully functioning gun.

sections.label: Anti-drone radar and jamming systems
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there are plans to develop Singapore's own anti-drone radar and jamming systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Are there plans to develop our own anti-drone radar and jamming systems?

sections.label: Training and standards for third-party licensing officers
sections.summary: The speaker asks what training third-party licensing officers will receive, what standards will be imposed, and how the Ministry will ensure adherence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: While I can understand the intent and need to optimise our resources, we must ensure that the third parties that are contracted are able to maintain the high standards of the MHA and SPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to ask what will be the training, if any, that will be provided to these third-party licensing officers, what are the standards that will be imposed on them, and how does the Ministry intend to ensure that they adhere to these standards.

sections.label: Clarifications on security clearances and Compliance Officers
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarifications on the provisions relating to security clearances and licensing and on the appointment of Compliance Officers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I would like to seek some clarifications on the provisions relating to security clearances and licensing and on the appointment of Compliance Officers.

sections.label: Private defence licences clarification
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether such considerations still apply and how many licences have been issued to individuals for private defence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry clarify whether such considerations still apply today and, if so, how many licences have been issued to individuals for this purpose of private defence?

sections.label: Compliance Officer minimum age
sections.summary: Non-compliance with a Compliance Officer's directions carries a fine of up to $10,000, and the Ministry is asked why the minimum age is 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Failure to comply with a Compliance Officer’s directions is also an offence punishable with a fine of up to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the powers and responsibilities of Compliance Officers are thus not trivial, could the Ministry explain why it decided to set the minimum age for Compliance Officers at only 18 years?

sections.label: Weapons information and 3D printing
sections.summary: Weapons and explosives information is more easily retrieved online, including the dark web, and 3D-printing enables customised creation of guns and weapons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Information on weapons and explosives can be more easily retrieved these days from the Internet, particularly from the dark web; new technology, such as 3D-printing, enables customised creation and manufacture of guns and other weapons.

sections.label: Upholding deterrence penalties
sections.summary: Singaporeans must be educated that this stand has been key to a secure and safe living environment, so deterrence penalties including capital punishment must be upheld.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: We must continue to educate Singaporeans that such a stand has been key to our secure and safe living environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Therefore, the deterrence penalties, in line with other relevant legislation, including capital punishment, must be upheld.

sections.label: AI against terrorism and weapons
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked how it would use AI to take pre-emptive measures against terrorism and the use of guns, explosives and weapons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: In this challenging digital environment, how would the Ministry use artificial intelligence or AI to take pre-emptive measures and strengthen our defence against terrorism and the use of guns, explosives and weapons?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Singapore is and will be a fair and equal society for all Singaporeans with zero tolerance of extremism.

sections.label: Global 3D printer numbers
sections.summary: Worldwide there are currently over 1.4 million 3D printers, estimated to rise to more than eight million units by 2027.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Worldwide, there are currently an excess of 1.4 million 3D printers, and the figure is estimated to rise to more than eight million units by 2027.

sections.label: Printing ammunition under future legislation
sections.summary: Clause 4 will ensure that printing ammunition falls under tight legislation if the technology emerges in future.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the printing of ammunition remains rudimentary and generally impotent at the moment, clause 4 of the bill will appropriately ensure that, if the technology to do so does emerge in the future, these will thereafter fall under tight legislation.

sections.label: Controlling firearms and digital blueprints
sections.summary: Clauses 12 and 13 make unauthorised digital gun blueprints illegal, but banning such items will be more limited than before.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, it is our responsibility to at least consider how, compared to the past when tight monitoring and policing was often sufficient, future attempts to control the spread of firearms will be that much more challenging.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thus, even when we widen the scope of controlled goods, as clauses 12 and 13 seek to do, by designating the manufacture and possession of unauthorised digital gun blueprints as illegal, we need to recognise that the act of simply banning such items will be more limited than before.

sections.label: Resourcing agencies and re-examining expenditure
sections.summary: Agencies should be resourced accordingly, with welfare and social services expenditure examined and domestic security spending re-examined if needed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If we believe this to be true, then we should be prepared to resource our agencies accordingly, to examine whether there is room to increase our expenditure for welfare and social services, and if budget considerations preclude otherwise, to re-examine our existing expenditure on publicly-funded domestic security services.

sections.label: Purchasing sophisticated 3D printers
sections.summary: A sophisticated 3D printer can be bought for under $5,000 from online portals and delivered within a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For the more serious hobbyist, a sophisticated 3D printer can be purchased under $5,000 for all your DIY needs from online portals such as Lazada and Amazon – and you can even have it delivered to your doorstep within a week.

sections.label: GrabCAD CAD models and weapons
sections.summary: GrabCAD has over 4.5 million CAD models, some for guns or weapons defined by the Bill, and 3D printing brings manufacturing opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: GrabCAD, an open source forum for 3D models has more than 4.5 million computer aided design models – more commonly known as CAD models – and a number of these designs are for guns or weapons as defined by the Bill, which includes knuckledusters, daggers, swords and nunchakus. 3D printing brings exciting opportunities in manufacturing.

sections.label: US shutdown of gun design site
sections.summary: US authorities shut the site down after the gun design had been downloaded 100,000 times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: When the US authorities got wind of it, they managed to shut the site down but not before the gun design had been downloaded a total of 100,000 times.

sections.label: Digital gun blueprints possession
sections.summary: The speaker supports clause 13, which covers unauthorised possession of digital blueprints for guns and major gun parts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In clause 13, I support the unauthorised possession of digital blueprints for guns and major parts of a gun.

sections.label: Pasir Ris knuckleduster fine appeal
sections.summary: A Pasir Ris resident appealed to the speaker against a Singapore Customs fine and confiscation for buying a knuckleduster online from overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: One of our Pasir Ris residents came to see me to appeal against the fine he received – including the confiscation of the item – from Singapore Customs for buying a knuckleduster online from an overseas source.

sections.label: Charging 3D printed weapon suppliers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes considering charging persons or companies supplying 3D printed weapons used in Singapore, along with the individual user.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As a deterrent and to ensure responsible 3D printing, I would like to propose that if 3D printed items are found to be used as weapons in Singapore, we should consider options to charge the person or company for supplying the weapons together with the individual that uses it.

sections.label: Education on responsible 3D printing
sections.summary: The speaker proposes enforcement plus education for responsible 3D printing, noting some five-axis CNC machine centres face export control, serialisation and yearly declarations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given the changing circumstances on making GEWs using 3D printers, I would like to propose a holistic approach of not only enforcement but also education to instill responsible 3D printing practices to the users and institutions that acquire these devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Some five-axis computer numerical control (CNC) machine centres are classified under export control, are serialised and also have yearly declarations as they are capable of manufacturing components for the centrifuge in building nuclear devices or ballistic missiles.

sections.label: Zero tolerance and 3D printing threat
sections.summary: The speaker says zero tolerance kept Singapore safe, but 3D printing threatens security, and supports the Bill while urging speed without over-criminalising 3D printing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In English): In conclusion, Mr Speaker, Sir, our zero tolerance for gun and weapon possession has been instrumental in keeping Singapore safe and keeping gun and weapon crimes to as low as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, our safety and security is now threatened by the unscrupulous use of the latest 3D printing technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We need to move quick and catch up with the technological threat that 3D printing poses without over-criminalising it and stifling 3D printing activities while continuing to maintain zero tolerance for gun or weapon possession in our country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Not withstanding the considerations I have proposed, I stand in support of the Bill.

sections.label: Tighter gun control and higher fines
sections.summary: The speaker supports tighter control over guns, explosives and weapons, fivefold higher maximum fines, and criminalising unauthorised possession of digital gun blueprints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Situations escalate quickly in territories where guns, explosives and weapons are accessible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I strongly support measures to tighten control over guns, explosives and weapons which pose higher risks as well as increasing the maximum fines for unlicensed activities fivefold to $50,000 for persons and $100,000 for entities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What has stood out for me in this Bill is the criminalisation of the unauthorised possession of digital blueprints for the manufacture of guns or major gun parts.

sections.label: Spotting mislabeled weapon parts
sections.summary: A concern is how the Singapore Police Force will spot and identify gun or weapon parts imported in hard-to-detect bits mislabeled as something else.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A concern I have is how the Singapore Police Force is going to spot and identify gun or weapon parts which can imported into Singapore in hard-to-detect bits and pieces, deceptively mislabeled as something else.

sections.label: Regulating 3D printers, weapons
sections.summary: The member asks for details on regulating 3D printers to prevent misuse while not stifling innovation, and says the regulatory framework should be updated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In English): Lastly, I would like to ask for more details and updates about how the Ministry intends to control and regulate 3D printers to prevent their misuse, while keeping a balanced approach so as not to stifle innovation for other engineering purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The regulation of guns, explosives and weapons is important to the safety and security of Singaporeans, and our regulatory framework should be updated to account for changing technologies and threats.

sections.label: Specific numbers in fourth limb
sections.summary: The fourth limb refers to controlling 12 guns or major gun parts, and these specific numbers seem to provide an opening to circumvent the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The fourth limb refers specifically to controlling or managing 12 guns or major parts of a gun.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These very specific numbers seem to provide an opening for someone to circumvent the law by possessing an explosive for only 23 hours or controlling only 11 guns.

sections.label: Licences for imitation weapons
sections.summary: The proposed Act appears to expand the law by requiring licences for imitation, replica and ornamental weapons, which existing laws do not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The result appears to be an expansion of the law, with the proposed Act requiring licences for imitation, replica and ornamental weapons, while existing laws do not.

sections.label: Compliance officers as private contractors
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Licensing Officer to appoint compliance officers to assist in enforcement powers, and these officers are private contractors, not public agents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill empowers the Licensing Officer to appoint compliance officers to assist the Licensing Officer in the exercise of its enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These compliance officers are private contractors, not public agents.

sections.label: Accountability of compliance officers
sections.summary: The member asks whether compliance officers will be held to the same accountability standards as public servants, and says this harmonises laws and strengthens enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will compliance officers be held to the same standards of accountability as public servants?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This effectively harmonises and updates the laws against new trends and threats and will strengthen the existing enforcement framework which will, in turn, minimise risks posed by GEW going forward.

sections.label: Shooting range licence security gap
sections.summary: The Bill requires the National Shooting Centre to operate under licence with tighter ammunition control and security to prevent arms leaving the range.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It did cross my mind then that a range user could leave the range with arms and live ammunition – in this scenario, the severity would be high, and the probability is low, although not zero.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill will now address this gap and require, for example, the National Shooting Centre, which is now not a licensable activity, to operate more securely under licence, such as tighter control of ammunition storage and issuance, for example, armed security at the range’s control points and better security measures in place to prevent firearms and ammunition leaving the shooting range.

sections.label: Class Licensing and GEW risk
sections.summary: The speaker notes school Air Gun Club members would not need individual licences and seeks assurance that Class Licensing will not cover higher risk GEW categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Examples include in the international arena, such as the SEA Games, ASEAN Games and at the International Shooting Sports Federation World Cup.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the Minister has highlighted that this Bill will mean that student members of a school’s Air Gun Club would now not be required to apply for individual licences, as this has always been a good source for scouting of young talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, as we have noted, the risk of GEW is low but not zero.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister can give us the continued assurance that the Class Licensing regime will not apply to the higher risk GEW categories or situations.

sections.label: 3D printing in Nerf community
sections.summary: About half of the estimated 5,000-strong Nerf community own a 3D printer, and hobbyists modify blasters to fire foam darts at 150-200 feet per second.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the past couple of years, 3D printing has made itself a staple in the Nerf community, where about half of those in the estimated 5,000-strong community own a 3D printer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While store-bought blasters typically fire at about 80-100 feet per second, our resourceful hobbyists are known to modify blasters that propel their foam darts up to 150-200 feet per second.

sections.label: Gerald's 3D printing face shields
sections.summary: Gerald began 3D printing for a school robotics competition and during the pandemic printed face shields donated to the constituency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Gerald’s interest in 3D printing began when he had to print parts for a robotics competition in school and, since then, during the pandemic, he has put his 3D printing skills to good use as he printed face shields in bulk that were donated to our constituency to help reduce the spread of the virus.

sections.label: Colour copier controls comparison
sections.summary: Proposed controls on 3D printing reminded the speaker of controls placed on colour copiers from 1979 to the late 1990s.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Proposed controls on 3D printing activities reminded me of the controls we placed on colour copiers from 1979 to the late 1990s.

sections.label: Maker spaces and 3D printing community
sections.summary: Maker spaces let people realise designs in community, and the speaker warns the Bill should not shackle a novel community without addressing the actual threat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With an already active community eager to facilitate the free flow of ideas and pool resources for the furthering of their hobbies, initiatives toward visibility sharing of designs and builds would not be too far-fetched.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have already seen several maker spaces, which are public workshops with 3D printing capabilities, where people can come and realise their designs in community, tapping on one another's experiences and resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These spaces are also good opportunities for the education of budding 3D printing enthusiasts to uphold community guidelines such as the Nerf community's compromise on the realism of their blasters to prevent panic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Should this Bill fail to provide an answer for the actual threat it is seeking to defuse, we set a precedent for shackling any novel community at the slightest hint of danger.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This Bill must live up to the responsibility it seeks to hold over the 3D printing community, lest we end up fighting a battle that simply did not exist in the first place.

sections.label: AOA recognises gun possession offence
sections.summary: The AOA will recognise unlawful possession of a gun with criminal intent and impose aggravating circumstances for scheduled offences like rioting, kidnapping and robbery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: The AOA will now recognise the offence of an unlawful possession of gun with criminal intent and impose aggravating circumstances for scheduled offences such as rioting, kidnapping and robbery.

sections.label: Section 64(2) limits Minister's security directions
sections.summary: Section 64(2) curtails the Minister's power to issue a security direction for regulated activity, limiting it to cases where making or amending regulations is impracticable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Section 64(2) of the Bill curtails the powers of the Minister to issue a security direction for regulated activity and limits it to cases where it is impracticable in the circumstances of the particular case for the Minister to make or amend any regulations to effectively address any issue or perceived issue of public safety.

sections.label: Domestic violence police reports increase
sections.summary: Police reports relating to domestic violence in Singapore increased by 22% since last April during the circuit breaker period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: For example, in my earlier parliamentary speech, I have shared that police reports relating to domestic violence in Singapore had increased by 22% since last April during the circuit breaker period in Singapore.

sections.label: RAND paper on 3D printing
sections.summary: A 2018 RAND Corporation research paper stated 3D printing technology will accelerate proliferation of dangerous weapons and could result in more crimes and violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: A research paper published by the RAND Corporation in 2018 stated that 3D printing technology will accelerate the proliferation of dangerous weapons and could result in more crimes and violence.

sections.label: Offence to possess 3D gun blueprints
sections.summary: The new rules will make it an offence for people to possess the blueprints required to 3D print gun parts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The new rules will make it an offence for people to possess the blueprints required to 3D print gun parts.

sections.label: Police licensing of shooting ranges
sections.summary: The Bill allows Police to issue licences for ranges, with a class licensing regime for lower risk activities balancing tough approach with practicality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A few years ago, in 2017, the Police already had imposed measures to better control activities at these premises, including measures to make such premises more secure and to better control the type of weapons being used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill allows the Police to issue licences for ranges, which allows Police more flexibility to regulate how they will operate through the imposition of licence conditions and they would be able to ensure the most stringent conditions for the use of firearms in Singapore and to ensure that such firearms are not easily available outside.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The introduction of a class licensing regime for lower risk activities balances the generally tough approach with practicality.

sections.label: Rationalising and harmonising offences
sections.summary: The changes rationalise and harmonise offences across legislation, setting penalties by culpability and seriousness of harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The other changes largely involve the rationalisation and harmonisation of offences that existed across many different pieces of legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There were some inconsistencies in these previously, as different offences were covered by different rules and developed at different times, but the overall changes in this new legislation rationalises the penalties based on degree of culpability, which means that there will be higher penalties for intentional offences and less for unintentional ones, as well as seriousness of the harm, which means higher penalties for more dangerous weapons and where weapons are used to cause harm.

sections.label: Unlicensed 3D-printed gun offences
sections.summary: Under present law, producing a gun with a 3D printer without a licence commits at least two offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To be clear, under present law, if you produce a gun using a 3D printer without a licence, you are committing at least two offences: unlicensed manufacturing a gun and possession of an illegal gun.

sections.label: Clause 13 limited to guns
sections.summary: Clause 13 is limited to guns and major gun parts, assessed to pose the highest risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: But we are also careful to ensure the law is not over-reaching.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We have limited clause 13 to guns and major gun parts as we have assessed these to pose the highest risk, necessitating such strong controls.

sections.label: Other jurisdictions' 3D gun laws
sections.summary: Other jurisdictions have passed legislation dealing with the threat of 3D printing of guns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Other jurisdictions have also passed legislation that deal with the threat of 3D printing of guns.

sections.label: MHA and NERF guns
sections.summary: MHA does not regulate NERF guns today and does not plan to do so at this juncture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: MHA does not regulate NERF guns today, and does not plan to do so at this juncture.

sections.label: Import licence for 3D-printed guns
sections.summary: Importing a 3D-printed gun, whether metallic or not, still requires a licence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: First, to clarify, the import of a 3D-printed gun, whether metallic or not, still requires a licence.

sections.label: Thresholds for guns and explosives
sections.summary: Thresholds of 12 for guns and major gun parts and 24 continuous hours for explosives were set from MHA's operational assessment of increased risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The thresholds of 12 for guns and major gun parts, and 24 continuous hours for explosives and explosive precursors, were determined based on MHA's operational assessment of the increased risks associated with these higher quantities or longer time of GEW being held in one's possession.

sections.label: Imitation or replica weapons
sections.summary: Imitation or replica weapons are not regulated under the Bill as they are unlikely to cause injuries or death and pose too little risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Imitation or replica weapons are not regulated under the Bill, as these are unlikely to be effective in causing injuries or death, and therefore pose too little risk to warrant tight regulation.

sections.label: Ornamental weapons class licensing
sections.summary: Ornamental weapons are covered under the Bill, but possession and storage will be considered for class licensing as overall safety and security risk is low.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Ornamental weapons, however, are covered under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: But we also recognise that the overall safety and security posed by these items is low, as long as they are kept safely and securely within dwelling places for the purpose of display.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Therefore, possession and storage of these items will be considered for class licensing.

sections.label: New licensing model for operators
sections.summary: A new licensing model lets an applicant make one application to obtain different licences for related activities, at lower cost than individual applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In addition, to help manage costs for operators, we will introduce a new licensing model, where if an applicant seeks to conduct related activities, he will only need to make one application to the regulator, to obtain the set of different licences for these activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The cost of this one application will be lower than the total of having to apply individual licences for each regulated activity.

sections.label: Close associate equity threshold
sections.summary: The 5% equity interest or voting rights threshold for a close associate is similar to a substantial shareholder under the Companies Act and used by Police.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The threshold of 5% equity interest or voting rights to qualify as a close associate is similar to that for determining a "substantial shareholder" under the Companies Act, and is currently used by the Police for the purpose of evaluating the fit and proper criteria.

sections.label: Judicial review against security direction
sections.summary: The Bill contains no privative or ouster clause, so a person aggrieved by exercise of power can seek judicial review against a security direction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To Mr Zhulkarnain's question on whether it is possible to seek judicial review against a security direction, given that a security direction is non-appealable under the Act, the Bill does not contain a privative or ouster clause, and so yes, a person who is aggrieved by exercise of power can seek judicial review.

sections.label: Imitation gun crime statistics
sections.summary: Nine imitation gun cases were reported in the last 10 years, with seven convictions under the Arms Offences Act or Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked for the statistics on crimes involving imitation guns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: There are only a handful of such cases – nine cases were reported in the last 10 years, of which seven resulted in conviction for offences under the Arms Offences Act or the Penal Code.

sections.label: Gun possession licences in force
sections.summary: There are currently 19 gun possession licences in force, issued to personal security officers of certain embassies for security and protection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked the question for the number of gun possession licences issued for self-defence that are still in force.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: There are currently 19 gun possession licences in force, issued to personal security officers of certain embassies, for security reasons and protection.

sections.label: Weapon-mounted drone threat response
sections.summary: SPF will work with CAAS on the weapon-mounted drone threat, as section 7B of the Air Navigation Act makes carrying prohibited items on drones an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: SPF will work closely with CAAS to deal with the threat of weapon-mounted drones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: This is because section 7B of Air Navigation Act today makes it an offence to operate a drone with prohibited items carried on it.
